correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact simplex facet volume, Cauchy shadow formula, crossed-edge sign count, sharp sign-class bounds and every-attainable-value via connectedness. Verified spherical absolute-product identity and finite exact moments, then established the joint limit using centered Gaussian signs and absolute-value sums, with uniform moving-threshold and normalization errors; odd/even Gaussian influence functions are orthogonal, giving independent Gaussian limits, and squaring gives the chi-square component. Standalone checker passed independent ConvexHull, finite envelope, moment quadrature and Monte Carlo tests; numerical tests are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The new claim is not that central section vertex counts, Haar normalization, Cauchy projection formulas, or Gaussian parity arguments are individually new. It is their sharp complete geometric coupling for arbitrary sign counts and the precise two-observable same-orientation joint limit, with exact shadow moments. Inspected closest full primary result texts establish only the separate marginal theorems. A complete published section-face-vector law is credited and not repackaged as new. Historical priority remains provisional because some earlier pertinent texts were accessible only as abstracts.
residual_risks: Full text of the 1992 random-regular-simplex projection study was inaccessible; an equivalent result under an older stereological formulation cannot be ruled out.
Full text of the 2020 König simplex section-volume paper was not inspected.
No web/database search can establish absolute historical uniqueness; two marginal ingredients are already published and credited.

value.rationale: Natural geometric coupling of simultaneously observed section complexity and perpendicular shadow size of the same regular simplex. Complete sign-stratified feasible domain, sharp equality class and exact shadow moments quantify a nontrivial combinatorial-to-metric constraint; independent Gaussian/chi-square limit demonstrates that constraint is not reflected as asymptotic dependence. This structural, all-dimensional classification and limiting phenomenon is more valuable than a textbook marginal computation or arbitrary numerical slice.
